title: The Roundabout (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 102bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist Perth driving
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The roundabout replaced the intersection in the nineteen nineties
And it was better in theory and occasionally in practice
You yield to the right and then you go and then you exit
The concept is straightforward and the reality complex

[Pre-Chorus]
I've lived in Perth for forty years and every roundabout surprises me
Someone always enters wrong and looks at me advisedly

[Chorus]
The roundabout knows something I don't know
It knows that circular is the only way some traffic flows
The roundabout removed the traffic light and gave us discretion
And human discretion at a roundabout is a philosophical question
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
Some people slow to a full stop and check all four horizons twice
Others enter at full speed and trust the other drivers' advice
The roundabout requires a social consensus formed at ten kilometres
Per hour between complete strangers — that's the theatre

[Bridge]
There is a five-roundabout system in Fremantle that I know
Which requires a map and a good relationship with the flow
I went around the outer one three times once in the rain
Before I found the exit — I was never the same again

[Outro]
Roundabout knows… human discretion is the variable… roundabout knows
That's my boy
